questions.q: To where did the man bring Ezekiel?
questions.a: The man brought Ezekiel back to the gate of the outer wall of the temple complex that faced east.

questions.q: What had been done to the east gate, and why?
questions.a: Yahweh says it must stay closed because he, Yahweh, the God of Israel, came in through it.

questions.q: Who is allowed to go into this east gate and eat in Yahweh’s presence?
questions.a: Only the one ruling Israel is allowed to go into the gatehouse and eat in Yahweh’s presence.

questions.q: What did Ezekiel see when the man brought him to the front of the temple building?
questions.a: Ezekiel saw that the light from the glory of Yahweh filled the temple.

questions.q: What was Ezekiel told to regarding the instructions and rules for the temple building?
questions.a: Ezekiel was told to watch, listen, and think carefully about all the instructions about the temple area.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the number of disgusting things the people of Israel have done?
questions.a: Yahweh says that the people of Israel have done too many disgusting things.

questions.q: What disgusting actions had the people of Israel done to defile Yahweh’s temple?
questions.a: The people of Israel had brought foreigners who did not obey Yahweh into his temple while they were offering sacrifices.

questions.q: Why did the people of Israel allow foreigners into Yahweh’s holy place?
questions.a: The people of Israel did not keep the duty of caring for Yahweh’s holy things. Instead, they put foreigners in charge of caring for his holy place.

questions.q: Who may not come into Yahweh’s holy place?
questions.a: No foreigner who is uncircumcised in heart and in flesh may come into Yahweh’s holy place, including the foreigners who live among the people of Israel.

questions.q: What had the Levites stopped doing?
questions.a: The Levites had stopped worshiping and obeying Yahweh and instead worshiped their idols.

questions.q: What had the Levites done?
questions.a: The Levites had helped the people of Israel to worship their idols.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say the Levites who stopped worshiping him may not do?
questions.a: Yahweh says that the Levites who stopped worshiping him may not serve as his priests, and they may not come near any of his most holy things.

questions.q: What was Yahweh going to assign the Levites to do?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would assign them to take care of the temple and to do all the work that is done in it.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh declare that the sons of Zadok would come near to him and would stand before him?
questions.a: The sons of Zadok would come near and stand before Yahweh because they kept the duties of Yahweh’s sanctuary when the people of Israel wandered away from him.

questions.q: Where must the sons of Zadok come near to serve Yahweh?
questions.a: They are the only ones who can come into Yahweh’s temple and draw near to his altar to serve him.

questions.q: What kind of clothes were the priests to wear when they came to the gates of the inner courtyard?
questions.a: The priests were to wear linen clothes and not wool when they enter the gates of the inner courtyard

questions.q: Why must the priests not wear woolen garments?
questions.a: The priests must not wear any material that will make them sweat.

questions.q: What must the priests do before they go out to the outer courtyard where the people gather?
questions.a: The priests must take off the garments they served in and lay them in the holy rooms. Then they must put on other garments.

questions.q: What must the priests do with their hair?
questions.a: The priests must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long. They must keep their hair trimmed.

questions.q: What may a priest not drink when he goes into the inner courtyard?
questions.a: A priest may not drink wine when he goes into the inner courtyard.

questions.q: Whom may a priest marry?
questions.a: A priest may marry a virgin who descended from the people of Israel, or a widow whose husband was a priest.

questions.q: What differences must the priests teach the people?
questions.a: The priests must teach the people the difference between what is holy and what is common and between things that are acceptable to Yahweh and things that are not acceptable to him.

questions.q: What is the role of the priests in a dispute among the people?
questions.a: The priests must stand to judge the dispute. They must judge what is right and wrong according to Yahweh’s laws.

questions.q: Who are the only dead people which a priest may touch and therefore make himself unclean?
questions.a: A priest may make himself unclean by touching the dead body of his father, his mother, his son, his daughter, his brother, or a sister who has never married.

questions.q: How long must a priest wait after his cleansing before he can again serve in the temple?
questions.a: The priest must wait seven days after his cleansing before serving in the temple.

questions.q: What must a priest present on the day he goes into the inner courtyard to serve in the Holy Place?
questions.a: He must present his sin offering.

questions.q: Why do the priests not receive any land or inheritance in Israel?
questions.a: The priests do not receive any land or inheritance in Israel because Yahweh is their inheritance and will provide all they need.

questions.q: What are the priests allowed to eat?
questions.a: The priests are to eat whatever is presented as the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.

questions.q: What part of their dough must the people give to the priest?
questions.a: The people must give the first batch of dough to the priest, so that everyone in their house would be blessed.

questions.q: What may the priests not eat?
questions.a: The priests may not eat any bird or animal that died on its own or that was killed by wild animals.

commentary.text: This chapter contains ordinances relative to the true priests. The prince evidently means Christ, and the words in Ezek. 44:2, may remind us that no other can enter heaven, the true sanctuary, as Christ did; namely, by virtue of his own excellency, and his personal holiness, righteousness, and strength. He who is the Brightness of Jehovah's glory entered by his own holiness; but that way is shut to the whole human race, and we all must enter as sinners, by faith in his blood, and by the power of his grace.
